name: Commander precon value (ramp, engines, one removal a turn)
description: The politics-free Commander baseline: a preconstructed-style deck that ramps on turns 2–3, lands its commander on turn 4, draws two cards a turn from an engine, points one removal spell at your best permanent each turn, and wraths on turn 6 when the board gets scary. Teaches which of your pieces to expose first and when a Commander table will sweep.

turns.boardSummary: Command Tower, Sol Ring: three mana available next turn

events.note: Turn-1 Sol Ring: they are a turn ahead of curve for the rest of the game.

turns.boardSummary: 2 lands, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet: five mana next turn
3 lands + 2 rocks; Cultivate fetched a basic and put one in hand

events.note: Land ramp does not die to a sweeper. By turn 4 they have seven mana.

turns.boardSummary: Commander on the battlefield, seven mana, removal held up

events.note: Cast from the command zone (CR 903.8). Expect it back every time it dies, taxed by two more mana each cast.
One white mana, instant speed, exiles your best creature at your end step.
events.breakPoint: Decision point: they hold up one white on your turn. Lead with the creature you can afford to lose and keep the engine piece until they tap low.

events.note: Your best creature is exiled; you gain life equal to its power.

turns.boardSummary: Card-draw engine online, drawing two extra cards a turn

events.note: Two extra cards a turn. From here the precon out-cards you unless your line ends the game.
events.breakPoint: Removal on the engine is worth more than removal on the commander; the commander comes back, the engine does not.

events.note: Three-mana instant that destroys any permanent and gives its controller a 3/3 Beast. It will hit your most important noncreature piece.
Your permanent is destroyed; you get a 3/3 green Beast token.

turns.boardSummary: Wrath of God: every creature dies; the table rebuilds from hand

events.note: Four-mana sweeper: destroy all creatures, they can't be regenerated. Enchantment- and artifact-based engines survive.
events.breakPoint: Decision point: a Commander table sweeps around turn 6. Hold two creatures back, or win before this turn, or make the sweeper hurt them more (death triggers, tokens that come back).

turns.boardSummary: Commander recast, the engine still drawing; they take over unless you rebuild faster

events.note: Commander tax: two more mana than last time (CR 903.8).

turns.boardSummary: Commander attacking every turn; the engine keeps them ahead on cards
